result:
The proposed answer is wrong. The claim that the HRS square attains the bound binom(t+1,2) is not justified, and the case s = 1 gives a counterexample.

When s = 1, HRS_t({α_i}, 1) is the ordinary Reed-Solomon code of length r and dimension t. Its Schur square is spanned by evaluations of products f·g with deg f, deg g ≤ t−1, so it consists of evaluations of polynomials of degree ≤ 2t−2. That space has dimension 2t−1, and the hypothesis t ≤ (r+1)/2 gives 2t−1 ≤ r, so the evaluation map is injective. Hence dim(C⋆2) = 2t−1 in this case.

The proposed formula gives binom(t+1,2) instead. For t = 3 (allowed when p ≥ 3 and r ≥ 5), it gives 6, but the true value is 5. The symmetric-square bound is not attained, because the products satisfy linear relations that the bound ignores.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
